details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has reduced its 2026 global growth projection to 3.0%, citing persistent risks from the ongoing war in the Middle East, increased trade fragmentation, and potential adjustments in market expectations for artificial intelligence. Despite some offsetting momentum from AI-driven demand in the technology sector, the IMF notes that global disinflation has stalled. The updated outlook warns of continued downside risks from renewed conflict, which could lead to commodity price volatility and tighter financial conditions worldwide.
title: IMF Lowers 2026 Global Growth Forecast Amid Mideast War

details: Global central bank interest rates are expected to remain elevated for an extended period, potentially rising by as much as half a percentage point through 2028, according to Bloomberg Economics. This revised outlook is largely influenced by lingering inflation risks stemming from the energy shock caused by the Middle East conflict and the ongoing race in artificial intelligence. Central banks, maintaining hawkish stances due to recent inflation surges, are contributing to a period of more expensive loans and mortgages for consumers and businesses globally.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Signal Higher Global Interest Rates

details: Digital asset markets have experienced a retreat following renewed geopolitical tensions, including US airstrikes on Iran. Both crypto equities and mining operations saw declines alongside broader technology stocks, as spot cryptocurrency markets eased due to a general "risk-off" sentiment among investors. This market reaction highlights the sensitivity of the cryptocurrency sector to global political instability, often prompting investors to move away from more speculative assets during times of uncertainty.
title: Geopolitical Risk-Off Sentiment Leads to Crypto Market Retreat
